character_facts: Aghnar can control or endure suffering to an extraordinary degree.
Aghnar loses his original feet and receives metal replacements.
Aghnar is addressed affectionately by someone overseeing or assisting the procedure.
Aghnar is identified as important to the future beginning of the Metabaron lineage.
The framing storyteller appears disciplined and focused on duty despite the listener's curiosity.
The listener is eager for lurid details about prior events and reacts with comic frustration when denied them.

An off-panel or framing storyteller/listener pair continuing the larger narration
The current Metabaron (mentioned, not clearly shown on the page)
continuity_links: This page presents Aghnar's mutilation as an origin point in the customs of the Metabaron line.
The bottom captions and dialogue explicitly set up continuation in the next episode/story segment.
The interrupted conversation indicates this page belongs to a larger framed retelling of Metabaron family history.
dialogue_meaning: A speaker tells Aghnar to stop self-mutilating because he has already proven mastery over suffering.
Aghnar is told that enduring pain is necessary because the machine stops only when there is nothing left for it to crush.
The narration frames this event as the moment Aghnar earned metal prosthetic feet.
The caption claims the prostheses make him heavier and stronger, tying bodily mutilation to the Metabaron lineage's ritual tradition.
A companion says Aghnar will walk again and links his survival to the future of the Metabaron line.
The framing conversation shifts abruptly from gruesome lore to household or work obligations because their master may return.
The listener wants more scandalous details about another episode, but the storyteller postpones the rest until tomorrow.
locations: A medical or mechanical chamber where Aghnar is operated on
An industrial or domestic service area connected to the storytellers
An exterior or windowed view of a futuristic city/structure with a hovering craft
lore_facts: Aghnar earns metal prosthetic feet through an ordeal of pain and mutilation.
These prosthetic feet are said to increase his weight.
The same augmentation is said to grant Aghnar superhuman powers.
Mutilation is described as one of the key components of Metabaronic initiation.
The Metabaron lineage is treated as a formal hereditary line with ritualized suffering.
There is a current Metabaron whose return causes subordinates to fear interruption or punishment.
plot_events: Aghnar undergoes a brutal operation or initiation involving severe pain and bodily mutilation.
The procedure results in Aghnar receiving metal prosthetic feet.
A narration box states that this suffering also grants him increased weight, superhuman power, and that mutilation becomes part of Metabaronic initiation.
After the procedure, attendants comfort or carry Aghnar while saying he will walk again.
The in-story narrators are interrupted because the current Metabaron may return soon.
One speaker refuses to continue the tale until later, emphasizing their work duties and the need for precision and punctuality.
A hovering craft approaches or is shown outside as the interruption lands comedically.
uncertainties: The exact identities and names of the attendants physically handling Aghnar are not stated clearly on this page.
Some dialogue in the lower framing conversation is small and could be misread in detail, though the overall meaning is clear.
The flying object in the final panel may indicate the current Metabaron's return, but the page does not explicitly label it in-panel.
visual_summary: In a surgical or workshop-like interior, an older white-haired man with cybernetic attachments is shown enduring extreme pain during a mechanical procedure. Blood drips from a machine in one panel, while attendants in fitted suits restrain and support him in another. A caption explains that he gains metal prosthetic feet through this ordeal. In the lower half, the patient is cradled by companions after the operation, and a close-up shows detailed metal feet. The page ends with servants or attendants interrupting the storytelling because the current Metabaron may return, followed by a hovering vehicle outside and a comic punchline about the interruption.
